title: Stratix POC - Quality & Benchmark Kickoff
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week POC focused on quality evaluation: define golden prompts, regression suite, hallucination checks, scoring rubric, plus load targets and timeline. Agreement to run small synthetic benchmarks, then 24/7 nightly regression runs; Redwood to provide example eval harness and initial cost estimate.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hi everyone, thanks for joining. i'm jordan, account exec for redwood inference. um we'll kick off — quick intros?
[00:12] Evan (Stratix): evan here, cto. we run a realtime insights product, lots of short prompts and some long-form summarization.
[00:20] Marta (Stratix): marta, lead ml eng. i'll own the evals and benching on our side.
[00:27] Priya (Redwood): priya, solutions engineer. i'll handle the technical scoping and benchmarks.
[00:35] Samir (Stratix): samir, sre — i'll be involved for infra and vpc/network questions.
[00:41] Claire (Stratix): claire, product. i'll help define success metrics.
[00:47] Jordan (Redwood): great. objective today is to agree success criteria for the poc, workload size, and a quality eval plan: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, and scoring. also timeline.
[01:05] Evan: quick context — we currently call open endpoints. latency is a pain for low-latency features, cost is... well we spend a lot. goal is reduce p99 latency under 300ms for short prompts and have a clear quality baseline before switching.
[01:30] Marta: quality is critical. we need deterministic regression gating so any model change doesn't drift. hallucinations are specific problem for our summaries, they hallucinate dates and entities.
[01:45] Priya: ok, so two axes: econ/latency and quality/regressions. for the poc, suggested scope: a golden set of 150 prompts (mix short queries & long summary tasks), a regression harness of ~2k examples for nightly runs, and targeted hallucination checks for the summary subset. does that map to your risk?
[02:10] Marta: 150 gold prompts sounds ok but we want them representative: 60 short, 60 mid, 30 long. also include 20 adversarial prompts.
[02:25] Jordan: noted. timeline thoughts? we were thinking 6 weeks total: week 0 onboarding + sample runs, week 1-2 synthetic and perf bench, week 3 ingested golden set and quality baseline, week 4 regression runs + threshold tuning, week 5-6 pilot/validation and final report.
[02:45] Evan: 6 weeks is fine as long as we get nightly runs and a clear go/no-go by end of week 5.
[03:00] Priya: on benchmarks: for performance we'll run both single-request p99 tests and sustained throughput tests. you mentioned ~600 qps peak for short prompts, is that still accurate?
[03:14] Samir: our traffic patterns — bursty: peaks around 500-700 qps for short in our busiest region, sustained 50 qps. we need recommendation for dedicated vs hosted.
[03:26] Priya: recommended path: start hosted for speed, run baseline. if p99 can't meet 300ms under your burst profile, we propose Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity for the peak and autoscale. we'll model cost in the POC.
[03:45] Marta: data constraints: we can't send full customer PII to hosted, some data must be filtered or tokenized. what are your options for private deployment or VPC?
[03:56] Alex (Redwood): Redwood Private (VPC) is available; for the POC we can run a hybrid: sanitized payloads to hosted for perf, and a VPC run for a smaller sample with raw data to validate outputs. we support KMS and audit logs.
[04:16] Claire: on success criteria: product wants p99 < 300ms for short prompts, mean latency < 700ms for long summaries, hallucination rate < 2% on the summary subset measured by our oracle, and automated regression pass rate >= 98%.
[04:38] Jordan: to clarify hallucination metric: is that fraction of outputs containing a fabricated fact per your labelers?
[04:45] Claire: yes, exact. we'll define label schema.
[04:50] Priya: ok scoring approach suggestions: weighted rubric. example: BLEU/ROUGE not great for open generation; use embedding-based semantic similarity + token-level hallucination checks + human spot checks. propose automated score = 0.6*semantic_similarity + 0.3*(1 - hallucination_rate) + 0.1*format_compliance.
[05:20] Marta: embedding sim — what embedding model? consistency matters for nightly runs.
[05:26] Priya: we can standardize on a single embed model (redwood-embed-xx or open-sim-3) for consistency; we'll ship the compute cost estimates.
[05:40] Evan: regression suite — do we need to provide labels or can you do automated fuzzy checks?
[05:48] Alex: mix: you'll provide golden labels for the 150 gold prompts; for the larger regression set, we can bootstrap with heuristics and then you annotate failing cases. nights runs will surface regressions and reduce label burden.
[06:05] Samir: infrastructure — we need to simulate burst traffic to emulate 700 qps for short prompts. how will you handle warm-up and KV cache effects?
[06:16] Priya: good call — we'll simulate realistic sequences with session stickiness to keep KV cache behavior. the perf harness will include cold-start scenarios and warmed-cache runs.
[06:30] Claire: hallucination checks — we need format checks for dates, currency, and entity consistency. sometimes model outputs lists with wrong bullet formatting which our downstream parser chokes on.
[06:44] Priya: we'll add format regex checks and structured parsing assertions to the eval harness; also a hallucination detector that flags invented dates/entities. it won't be perfect but will catch many regressions.
[07:02] Jordan: does anybody use reranking or few-shot templates today?
[07:07] Marta: we use few-shot in prompts for summaries. golden prompt design must include those templates.
[07:14] Priya: we'll capture prompt templates and seed examples. golden prompts will include prompt + expected output example and acceptance criteria.
[07:24] Evan: scoring thresholds — if nightly regression falls below 98% pass we want an alert and a rollback policy. how does redwood support rollbacks?
[07:36] Alex: Redwood rollouts support canary and automatic fallback to previous model bundle if quality drops beyond threshold. we can wire alerts into your pager.
[07:50] Samir: security question — logs and request traces with PII redaction? also SOC2?
[07:58] Jordan: we have SOC2 Type II and support KMS for encryption at rest, SSO/SAML, and audit logs. we can share security docs after the call.
[08:10] Claire: timeline detail — what are deliverables each week?
[08:15] Priya: deliverables: week0 onboarding doc + configurations; week1 perf harness + initial perf report; week2 golden prompt list + baseline quality; week3 regression harness with 2k examples + nightly runs; week4 threshold tuning and canary config; week5 pilot validations + cost model; week6 final report and decision meeting.
[08:38] Evan: ok. cost — high level estimate?
[08:42] Jordan: we'll send a preliminary estimate: hosted token cost + optional reserved dedicated cost. for the poc we'll provide cost-range scenarios in the follow-up.
[08:52] Marta: on evaluation tooling — can you share an example harness or notebook?
[08:56] Priya: yes, we'll share a sample eval repo (link in follow-up). includes runner, metric scripts, and hallucination regex suite.
[09:05] Claire: about golden prompts: who curates them?
[09:09] Marta: we can propose initial set but want redwood to review and augment with adversarials.
[09:15] Jordan: agreed: we'll collaborate on golden set; action item for both sides.
[09:20] Priya: quick note about regression cadence — nightly runs ok? or do you prefer hourly smoke tests?
[09:26] Samir: nightly is ok, plus hourly smoke for critical endpoints.
[09:31] Evan: success criteria recap?
[09:33] Claire: p99 < 300ms short, mean < 700ms long, hallucinations < 2%, regression pass >= 98%.
[09:41] Jordan: great. next steps...
[09:44] Priya: i'll spin up perf harness and share template by tuesday; jordan will send security docs and cost sketch; marta and team to share anonymized sample payloads and initial golden prompt candidates by end of week.
[10:00] Marta: we'll try to get 150 gold prompts by friday.
[10:05] Evan: schedule a check-in after week2 perf report.
[10:09] Jordan: ok. any other Qs?
[10:12] Claire: curious if you support automated hallucination patch rules — like forced nil for dates when model uncertain?
[10:20] Alex: we provide post-processing hooks you can plug for format enforcement and safe defaults. that's part of Redwood Optimize recommendations.
[10:30] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with docs and links. rough end time — thanks, bye.
